title: Drag policy — what it actually is
summary: Zach: "This is not entirely true." He is right. One clause of the hosts lane's claim measured true, one is a third of the real policy and wrong for every non-container view, and one measured outright false. The requirement underneath it — a cold press-and-drag moves the thing — is already satisfied by stock React Flow; what is missing is the grab AREA and any notion of hover/selected at all.
changes: apps/storybook-basics/src/interaction/dragPolicy.ts — the contract: three roles (grab / inert / owns-pointer), the per-component declarations as data, resolveGrab (nearest-declaration-wins), resolveClick (the donor's one rule), the gesture table, and every threshold with its donor citation.
apps/storybook-basics/src/interaction/dragIntent.ts — press → click|drag as a pure reducer. No React, no DOM, no timer.
apps/storybook-basics/src/interaction/grabChain.ts — the host half: the DOM walk, the attribute names, and the nodrag bridge to React Flow's stock filter.
apps/storybook-basics/src/interaction/useDragIntent.ts — the React binding. Listener plumbing only.
apps/storybook-basics/src/interaction/policyStage.tsx — the shared story stage: declaration table + live React Flow canvas + a live hover readout resolved through the real walk.
apps/storybook-basics/src/stories/DragPolicy.stories.tsx — 9 stories, each with a play that drives real pointer+mouse sequences and measures getBoundingClientRect.
Nothing under src/components/** was touched — a concurrent lane owns those files. Every wiring change is listed under “Owed wiring” below instead.
findings:
1 · The verdict on the disputed sentence

The claim, from commit 4ada3f8: “Per-type policy fell out cleanly: block drags by its header, Code and Value editors are nodrag, glyph drags by its whole face.” Each clause, measured in a real Chromium tab through the Playwright gate — press, eight move events, release, then the node's own getBoundingClientRect delta:

ClauseVerdictThe measurement behind it
“block drags by its header”PARTLY TRUE of the code, wrong as policyHeader: moved 49.9px ✓. Footer band: 0px. Port-label text: 0px. The 4px edge-to-words strip: 0px. And a view: "port" block (sink), which the donor makes a solid face, moved 0px from its interior. Header-only is one of three donor bands for an expanded Block, and flatly wrong for every other view.
“Code and Value editors are nodrag”TRUECode editor interior: 0px. Value editor interior: 0px. The mechanism is confirmed in React Flow's own filter — @xyflow/system@0.0.82/dist/esm/index.mjs:2352. The residual grab area for a code node is the wrapper's 10px ring (reactFlowHost.tsx:227), measured grabbable at 49.9px — and a 10px target.
“glyph drags by its whole face”FALSEA press on the centre of the rendered face moved the node 0px; a press on the node's 1px margin moved it. The centre resolves to the lucide <svg><path>. Nothing on that ancestor chain carries nodrag and nothing has pointer-events: none, so React Flow's filter should have passed it — cause unresolved, reported as measured-but-unexplained.

2 · Three findings the claim did not mention, and one of them is bigger than the claim

A plain click never selects anything.applyPositionChanges (reactFlowHost.tsx:323-332) keeps only change.type === "position", so React Flow's select changes are dropped, and the host is controlled, so the store's flag is never authoritative. Measured: click on header / glyph / body → selected === false every time. Selection appears only as a side effect of drag start (@xyflow/system:2252-2254 writes the store directly). Zach asked for “hovered vs selected” — today neither state exists to show.
The threshold ordering is inverted.React Flow's nodeDragThreshold is left at its default of 1 (@xyflow/react@12.11.6/dist/esm/index.mjs:3331) while the dnd-kit rails in the same tree arm at 4. So the canvas — the outermost, least specific owner — claims a contested press 3px before the rail ever sees it. SystemSketch does the opposite on purpose: “Strictly below tldraw's own drag-start threshold (4 screen px … ), so the claim preempts pointing_shape → translating rather than racing it” (memberStackDnd.tsx:89-94). The repo is saved from this today only by spatial exclusion, which is the thing measured to be incomplete.
A member's header drags its parent.React Flow implements dragHandle by walking ancestors from the press target to the node root and matching the selector anywhere on the chain (hasSelector, @xyflow/system:2038-2048). A member Block's header matches the parent's [data-slot="block-header"], so pressing the child drags the parent — measured, kid's header moved proc 40.8px. Inheritance by ancestor-matching is the bug; it is exactly why the design below stops the walk at the nearest declaration.

3 · The requirement is already met — by the engine, not by us

“generally where I just 1 click and drag I want it to move, even if it hasn't been selected prior, you need to sense the click and drag motion...”
— /home/bam/zach_brain/Projects/bbox-ui/PROJECT - Black Box UI.md:2504

Read from React Flow's own source, getDragItems admits a node when node.selected || node.id === nodeId (@xyflow/system:2053) — the || is the whole answer. Measured: every successful drag in this lane ran with selected === false beforehand. So this is not an intent-detection gap. It is a grab-area gap plus a missing selection model, and framing it as “add drag sensing” would have built the wrong thing. One real defect does sit here though: React Flow's startDrag sets its reference point at the threshold-crossing position (:2255-2256), so the node lags the pointer permanently by the first move event's delta — measured 49.9px for a 56.6px drag. With a real mouse that is 1–2px and reads as slight stickiness rather than a bug; dragDelta in this lane measures from the origin instead.

4 · What SystemSketch actually does — the donor policy, with citations

Deliberately NOT ported, and why: SystemSketch has three gesture owners that can each claim one press, documented and unfixed on main (tests/test_stock_boundary.py:280-318, “KNOWN GAP — these owners are NOT yet mutually exclusive”); the literal 3 is copy-pasted in six places with four different justifications; and five near-identical *ClickToEdit modules each carry their own copy of isPlainLeftClick. What is ported is the property their PEP names: owners are separated by which state owns the press, re-checked at claim time — never by timing (docs/peps/0013-two-scoped-canvas-drag-owners.md:36-38).

6 · The design — where the component/host line falls

Zach's instinct: “each component should defining its own behaviour … in the composite components you should just get the logic for free.” That is right about the declaration and wrong about the behaviour, and the difference is the measured member-header bug above. The repo's governing rule (CLAUDE.md, “The one rule the design rests on”) says interaction geometry is host-owned and never travels — so:

The component DECLARES (portable, travels to any host)The host IMPLEMENTS (never travels)
Which of its named parts (data-slot, which it already emits) are grab, inert, or owns-pointer, and what its bare face is. Which parts open an editor once it is already active. That is a set of facts about itself, in its own vocabulary — no engine import, no measurement, no listener, identical on DOM, React Flow and tldraw.Which element is under the pointer. The walk from that element to the nearest declaration. The click-vs-drag threshold and its ordering against inner owners. Pointer capture. The viewport transform and the delta ÷ zoom. Z-order. What “selected” means and where it is stored. The veto token (nodrag on React Flow, markEventAsHandled on tldraw).

Composition is nearest-declaration-wins, not inheritance. The walk stops at the first element carrying a declaration, so a member's declaration shadows its parent's. That single rule is simultaneously the fix for the measured leak and the mechanism that makes “free for composites” come out correct rather than accidental.

A parent may only narrow, never widen. Widening would let a parent claim a press over a child that owns its pointer — dragging the block instead of placing the caret in its code editor — which is the exact bug class nodrag exists to prevent, and it would make a component's declaration about its own internals non-authoritative. Narrowing's worst case is a surface that simply does not drag. An undeclared surface defaults to inert, never grab: a press that moves the wrong thing is worse than a press that moves nothing.

7 · The thresholds, and where each number comes from

ConstantValueProvenance — read on disk, not from memory
CANVAS_DRAG_INTENT_PX4 client pxtldraw's own dragDistanceSquared: 16 — /home/bam/systemsketch/node_modules/@tldraw/editor/dist-cjs/lib/options.js:36, @tldraw/editor 5.3.2.
CANVAS_DRAG_INTENT_COARSE_PX6 client pxcoarseDragDistanceSquared: 36 — same file, options.js:34. The touch answer.
INNER_CLAIM_PX3 client pxSTACK_DND_CLAIM_DISTANCE_PX, memberStackDnd.tsx:95, with its WHY at :89-94: “Strictly below tldraw's own drag-start threshold … so the claim preempts pointing_shape → translating rather than racing it. A press released under this distance is a plain click and never touches dnd-kit.”

The ordering is the load-bearing part, not the values. A unit test asserts INNER_CLAIM_PX < CANVAS_DRAG_INTENT_PX so the invariant cannot be tuned away by accident. Measured in client px, deliberately, so the threshold means the same amount of finger movement at every zoom — React Flow says so in its own source (@xyflow/system:2303: “Calculate distance in client coordinates for consistent drag threshold behavior across zoom levels”), and a zoom-1.75 measurement confirmed it: a 40px client drag moved the node 19.4 scene px, i.e. the delta is divided by zoom while the threshold is not. There is no zoom bug in the host's node drag.

And no long-press branch anywhere, on purpose: the donor spent a PEP establishing that tldraw's long_press does not mean “the press did not move” — it is a 500ms timer cleared by the drag-threshold move branch — so timing cannot separate gesture owners (docs/peps/0013-…md:39-47; SystemSketch now fails its own build if a comment claims otherwise, :87-88).

8 · Owed wiring — one line each, once the components lane clears

Nothing under src/components/** was edited: a concurrent lane owns every file there. These are the exact changes that make the running code match the policy above. The story stage injects data-drag-owner from outside today so the policy is demonstrable now; that scaffold (policyStage.tsx's attach) is meant to be deleted when this lands.

FileChange
hosts/reactFlowHost.tsx:291-297Delete DRAG_HANDLE_FOR_TYPE. A per-type selector cannot express a per-view policy, and the ancestor walk makes any selector leak into members. Replace with a noDragClassName-based boundary plus the component's own declaration.
hosts/reactFlowHost.tsx:350Drop dragHandle: DRAG_HANDLE_FOR_TYPE[…] from the node decoration.
hosts/reactFlowHost.tsx:368-379Add nodeDragThreshold={CANVAS_DRAG_INTENT_PX} (4). Today it is React Flow's default 1, which arms the canvas before every inner owner.
hosts/reactFlowHost.tsx:323-332applyPositionChanges must also carry select changes into host state (not necessarily into the scene record) — without it there is no selected state, so no “1 click then click-and-drag” and no hover/selected paint.

Add a data-slot="block-footer" band — bbox-ui's Block has no footer element at all today (measured: querySelector('[data-slot="block-footer"]') is null on both fixtures), so one third of the donor's grab area cannot exist yet.
components/blockPort.tsxEmit data-drag-owner="port" on each rail item, so a port's declaration shadows its block's and the dot/text split resolves locally.

components/portEdge.tsx (dnd-kit sensor)Lower activationConstraint.distance from 4 to INNER_CLAIM_PX (3), so the rail claims strictly before the canvas — the donor's ordering.

9 · What I could not verify

  • Why the glyph face centre does not drag. Measured repeatedly; the ancestor chain has no nodrag and no pointer-events: none, so React Flow's filter should pass. The <svg><path> target is the prime suspect and pointer-events: none on the SVG is the proposed fix, but I did not test that fix — it needs a component edit this lane is barred from making.
  • tldraw. Not implemented in this repo (deliberately cut from hosts phase 1 — it needs a ShapeUtil, a toolbar entry and frame interop), so every measurement here is React Flow only. Where tldraw would differ: the grab area becomes getGeometry (chrome bands as isLabel children, which is also how they stay out of marquee-select — blockSelectableArea.test.ts:201), and the veto becomes editor.markEventAsHandled instead of a class.
  • Touch. The coarse threshold (6px) is cited from tldraw's options and unit-tested, but never exercised with real touch events.
  • The two expect(...).toBe(0) assertions in BlockSolid and PortTextVsDot pin current, wrong behaviour on purpose, so the wiring landing makes them fail loudly rather than passing silently. They are the one place in this lane where green means “still broken”; the comment beside each says so.
  • The browser pane drifted onto port 5421 — Zach's live review server — during early exploration, and fired pointer events at whatever story it had open there. Harmless (Storybook writes nothing), but it is why every measurement in this report was re-taken through STORYBOOK_PORT=5491 pnpm test-stories instead, which cannot wander.

stories.look_for: The requirement itself. Grab the block's header with one press — it was never selected — and it moves. The note cites the line in React Flow's source that already makes this true.

stories.title: Block (expanded) · the disputed case
stories.look_for: The declaration table on the left, the live canvas on the right. Orange = grab, blue = the subtree owns the press, grey = inert. The donor's grab area is header ∪ port-label bands ∪ footer, not header alone.

stories.look_for: The face is declared grabbable because the donor makes every non-container view solid — and the play function measures that the running host still moves it 0px from the body. That assertion is the one that flips when the wiring lands.
